skill.name: backend-ralph-plan
skill.description: Creates structured plan directories for backend Django projects, including PLAN.md, task files, and RALPH-PROMPT.md for Ralph loop execution with quality gates.
skill.summary: Create Django backend implementation plans with task tracking, quality gates, and Ralph loop prompts.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, inline code formatting, local developer command templates, and double-brace placeholders. I found no evidence of malware, credential access, unauthorized network activity, obfuscation, or prompt injection attempts in the reviewed files. The skill still expects users to review generated shell commands before running Ralph plans.

remediation.issue: Generated plans include local shell commands for linting, tests, Django checks, git, and grep.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must review command values and paths before running the generated Ralph prompt in a repository.

remediation.issue: Template placeholders can be mistaken for obfuscation by automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder syntax documented and avoid dense placeholder-only examples when plain descriptions are enough.

remediation.issue: The skill allows Bash because generated workflows invoke project tooling.
remediation.suggestion: Limit Bash guidance to explicit local quality gates and avoid adding commands that fetch remote code or expose secrets.

content.value_statement: Large Django features can lose task order, quality gates, and progress context. This skill creates a plan directory and Ralph prompt for iterative implementation.
actual_capabilities: Creates a PLAN.md task index with status, execution order, progress, and quality gate tables.
Creates individual task files with goals, scope, dependencies, checklists, tests, completion criteria, and notes.
Creates RALPH-PROMPT.md for repeated Ralph loop execution against the generated plan.
Defines local verification commands for linting, type checks, Django checks, tests, coverage, and shortcut detection.
Supports custom Django app paths, module paths, test filters, tooling commands, coverage targets, and iteration limits.
Provides a complete user preferences example and reference templates for plan structure and quality gates.
limitations: Designed for backend Django projects, not frontend projects or general application planning.
Requires accurate user-provided task details, paths, test filters, and local tool commands.
Does not implement the feature itself; it creates the plan files and execution prompt.
Generated shell commands should be reviewed before running them in a repository.

use_cases.title: Plan a Django Feature
use_cases.description: Break a backend feature into ordered tasks with explicit verification gates and completion tracking.

use_cases.title: Prepare Autonomous Iteration
use_cases.description: Create a Ralph prompt that can repeatedly resume work, check status, run tests, and commit completed tasks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Capture consistent lint, type, test, coverage, Django, and shortcut checks for every task in a plan.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small Django backend feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a backend Ralph plan for a Django feature named User Preferences. Use four tasks: model, service, API, and caching. Use app path accounts/ and test filter preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tooling Details
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a backend Ralph plan for Billing Webhooks. Use .bin/ruff check, .bin/ruff format, .bin/ty, .bin/pytest, and .bin/django check. Set coverage target to 90 percent.

prompt_templates.title: Include Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for ordered implementation work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a backend Ralph plan for Audit Log Search. Include tasks for schema, indexing, service filters, API endpoints, permissions, and tests. Order tasks by dependency.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Large Codebase Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that needs orientation before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a backend Ralph plan for Organization Settings in a large Django codebase. Add a warm-up orientation task before implementation and include blockers guidance.

output_examples.input: Request a plan for a user preferences API with model, service, API, and caching tasks.
output: A plan directory with PLAN.md, RALPH-PROMPT.md, and four numbered task files.
A task order that starts with the model layer and ends with caching.
Quality gates covering lint, type checks, Django checks, tests, coverage, and shortcut detection.

output_examples.input: Request a plan for a complex backend feature in an unfamiliar Django app.
output: A warm-up orientation task that documents existing models, service patterns, and testing conventions.
Implementation tasks with dependencies and completion criteria.
A Ralph prompt that resumes progress from PLAN.md and git history.

output_examples.input: Request a Ralph-ready plan with custom local tool wrappers.
output: A generated plan using the requested wrapper commands for linting, formatting, tests, and Django checks.
Task tracker rows that record pass status for each quality gate.
A final completion promise tied to the exact task count and plan slug.

best_practices: Provide exact app paths, module paths, test filters, and local tooling commands before generating the plan.
Keep each task focused on one backend layer or feature slice with four to eight checklist items.
Review generated commands and task order before running the Ralph loop.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for quick prototypes that do not need iterative verification.
Do not create broad tasks that span many unrelated layers or require human decisions at every step.
Do not run generated shell commands until their paths and arguments have been reviewed.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a plan directory with PLAN.md, task files, and RALPH-PROMPT.md for Ralph loop execution.

faq.question: Is it only for Django projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The templates and examples assume backend Django structure, Django checks, pytest, and Python quality gates.

faq.question: Does it write application code?
faq.answer: No. It writes planning and prompt files that guide later implementation work.

faq.question: Can I customize the commands?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide project-specific lint, format, type check, test, Django, and coverage commands.

faq.question: How does Ralph use the generated prompt?
faq.answer: The plan runner reads RALPH-PROMPT.md, extracts the completion promise, and invokes the Ralph loop with that prompt.

faq.question: What should I review before running it?
faq.answer: Review generated paths, shell commands, task order, completion criteria, and any custom placeholders.
